South Korea Jet Lag & Sleep Shift Planner

Build a day-by-day light exposure, sleep adjustment, and caffeine cutoff plan tailored to your home time zone and arrival time in South Korea (UTC+9).

Beat South Korea jet lag faster. South Korea Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9 with no daylight saving time. Pick your home time zone, arrival time in South Korea, and usual bedtime to get a customized day-by-day light exposure, caffeine cutoff, and sleep-shift schedule starting 2 days before departure. Pair this with our First Day in South Korea Arrival Guide.

Your flight & sleep routine

Why South Korea jet lag feels different

  • North America → South Korea (crossing the date line westward): your body clock thinks 3:00 PM in Seoul is the middle of the night, and you'll wake up wide awake at 4:00 AM JST for the first two mornings. Lean into it—visit Senso-ji, Meiji Shrine, or Fushimi Inari at 6:00 AM before crowds arrive.
  • Europe → South Korea (flying east 7–9 hours): advancing your clock eastward is harder on the body. Seek morning outdoor light after 9:00 AM JST and avoid bright sunlight before 7:00 AM on Day 1 so you don't shift the wrong direction.
  • Hotel bath / onsen trick: a 15-minute warm soak at 9:30 PM raises core body temperature; the rapid cool-down afterward triggers natural sleepiness.
